title: "Every context switch flushes the TLB": true or a relic?

cast.name: Zed
cast.role: Repeats rules he read years ago

cast.name: Abi
cast.role: Kernel developer who reads the manual

glossary.note: A small cache of finished address translations.
An x86 tag on TLB entries, held in the low bits of CR3.
Holds the base of the page tables (and the PCID) on x86.
The arm64 tag on TLB entries.
Holds the arm64 page-table base and the ASID.

key_points: Without PCID, a CR3 write drops all non-global TLB entries.
With PCID or ASID tags, entries from different address spaces can coexist.
Setting bit 63 on the CR3 write tells x86 not to flush.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Zed types his rule about the TLB into a shared shell, as a comment.

visuals.cmd: # every context switch flushes the whole TLB

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Then why does this CPU advertise a feature for not flushing? It's called PCID.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This session is illustrative, as an x86 Linux box prints it. This reel was made on an arm64 Mac, which has no proc to read.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: The TLB caches translations, virtual page to frame.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Process A put page 0x400 in frame 0x91. Now we switch to process B, whose page 0x400 lives in frame 0x2c.
beats.say: Process A put page four hundred hex in frame ninety-one hex. Now we switch to process B, whose page four hundred lives in frame two C.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Untagged, B hits A's entry and reads the wrong frame. So the old answer was: flush.

steps.label: hit, but frame 0x91 is A's: wrong

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Without PCID, each write to CR3 on a switch drops every non-global entry, and the next accesses all miss.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: On CPUs without it. With PCID, the low twelve bits of CR3 tag every entry.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: So process B's entry moves in beside A's, instead of evicting it.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: The kernel source spells out the bits. Watch the last line.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Twelve bits of PCID. And bit sixty-three set on the CR3 write means: keep the old entries.

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: Arm tags entries with an ASID, kept in the TTBR. Its invalidates reach other cores by broadcast; this flag opts out.

out: 562:/* Perform the tlbi locally without broadcasting to other CPUs. */

beats.speaker: abi
beats.text: x86 sends interrupts to other cores instead. A flush is a choice, not a law.
